## Correctness

**PASS** — The free-algebra calculation is correct over an arbitrary field. For w in the subalgebra generated by the frozen variables, D_w replaces one occurrence of x_i by w and strictly lowers the x_i-count, so it is locally nilpotent. Abelianization sends D_w to the coefficient-wise image of w times partial_{x_i}; hence the kernel on these elementary LNDs is exactly the commutator ideal of the frozen free algebra. The degree-d kernel dimension is (n-1)^d minus the degree-d commutative monomial count, giving the stated Hilbert series. For n>=3, D(x_1)=[x_2,x_3], D(x_j)=0 is an explicit nonzero invisible LND. Combined with the rank-two zero-detection result of Baltazar--Lopes--Morales and the trivial rank-one case, this proves the stated sharp threshold over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field. No boundary-case defect was found.

## Originality

**PASS** — The recent Baltazar--Lopes--Morales preprint treats the rank-two free algebra and analyzes abelianization there; older Crode--Shestakov and Drensky--Makar-Limanov results concern rank-two triangulability and kernels, while the Drensky--Yu rank-three survey concerns automorphisms and coordinates. Targeted searches for the higher-rank abelianization threshold, the prototype coefficient [x_2,x_3], and the exact elementary-fiber/Hilbert-series statement did not locate a prior covering theorem. The mechanism is elementary and the novelty claim is therefore narrow: the pass is for the explicit sharp threshold and fiber description as a new synthesis, not for triangular LNDs or commutator ideals themselves.

## Scientific value

**PASS** — Although technically elementary, the result gives a sharp structural boundary for a property highlighted by the newest rank-two work: abelianization detects zero LNDs in rank two but already has an exponentially large invisible elementary-LND kernel from rank three onward. The affine-fiber description and graded dimension formula quantify the failure rather than merely exhibiting one example, making the statement a useful diagnostic for attempts to transfer rank-two LND phenomena to higher free rank.

## Sources

- A Characterization of Local Nilpotence for Derivations of Ore Extensions (Rene Baltazar; Samuel Lopes; Oscar Morales): https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.19470 — Current rank-two source; explicitly studies the free associative algebra and abelianization in characteristic zero.
- Locally nilpotent derivations and automorphisms of free associative algebra with two generators (Sidney Dale Crode; Ivan P. Shestakov): https://doi.org/10.1080/00927872.2020.1729363 — Proves rank-two triangulability; no higher-rank abelianization threshold is stated in the accessible abstract/metadata.
- Locally Nilpotent Derivations of Free Algebra of Rank Two (Vesselin Drensky; Leonid Makar-Limanov): https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.13262 — Rank-two kernel theory and uniqueness up to scalar from the kernel.
- Coordinates and automorphisms of polynomial and free associative algebras of rank three (Vesselin Drensky; Jie-Tai Yu): https://doi.org/10.1007/s11464-007-0002-9 — Rank-three automorphism/coordinate survey; no matching LND-abalianization theorem was located.

## Limitations

- The higher-rank construction is elementary, so equivalent folklore under different terminology remains a residual originality risk.
- The global iff statement invokes the cited rank-two characteristic-zero theorem; the explicit n>=3 construction itself works over any field.
- No classification of all higher-rank locally nilpotent derivations in the abelianization kernel is claimed.
